_notes: Active-learning ensemble-member config: a parametric ConcatLSTM, NOT the shipped HyperWaveNet.
The active-learning workflow is adapted from PANAMA (arXiv 2509.26564v1); the ConcatLSTM
conditioning scheme (encode the control vector, tile across time, concatenate to audio) is theirs.
Architecture, loss, and gamma follow PANAMA's published LSTM defaults (3 layers of 18 units,
MSE plus seven-resolution log-mel loss, ExponentialLR gamma 0.995), but the recurrent-gradient
path, learning rate, and warmup are set for the short single-file dataset used here:
lr 0.008 and 16 warmup epochs. train_truncate is null (full BPTT): every truncated
recipe tried on this capture generalized worse than the pre-truncation full-BPTT runs
at this batch size, whose logs show occasional non-finite gradients (survived by
configure_gradient_clipping's non-finite skip, not a crash) that are likely a bounded
catapult effect helping escape sharp minima.
This LSTM is a disposable query-by-committee acquisition proxy: scripts/active_learn.py trains a
4-member ensemble from this config to find the control settings where members disagree most.
ConcatLSTM derives its conditioning width (1 + encoded_param_dim) from the params below, so there
is no PANAMA-style 'conditioning_dim' key; the params block MUST match the production parametric
model you intend to capture for (here: the Gain/Tone/Boost example).
Physical batches are GPU-sized and gradient-accumulated to the effective batch of 37
(see nam_full_configs/active_learning/learning.json), smaller than PANAMA's 512.
val_loss picks the checkpoint to keep; it is not the training objective, which stays PANAMA's
MSE + log-mel. Stated explicitly because omitting it silently selects on MSE, and every other
parametric config here selects on ESR -- MSE weights the loud corner of the control space.
